method: extract-verify adjudication of 76 AI-direct blocked materiality rows vs primary local SEC filings (63 filings; skeptical default-exclude)

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuer); Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC (Initial Purchaser); Wilmington Trust, N.A. (Trustee)
decisions.recourse: N/A - basis figure unsupported by filing
decisions.rationale: The ~$73.27B basis appears nowhere in the filing; the only committed obligation disclosed is the $3.2B notes, so this inflated aggregate has no matching specific committed principal.
decisions.source_quote: The aggregate principal amount of notes sold in the offering was $3.2 billion.

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuer, TeraWulf indirect subsidiary); Wilmington Trust, N.A. (Trustee); Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC (Initial Purchaser); TeraWulf and Guarantors (guarantors)
decisions.recourse: Senior secured obligations of WULF Compute LLC, guaranteed by TeraWulf and the Guarantors, plus a TeraWulf completion guarantee for the Data Center Expansion
decisions.rationale: $3.2B of 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 were actually issued/completed at 100% of principal under an executed indenture to finance the Lake Mariner data center expansion - a specific, committed AI-infrastructure debt obligation.
decisions.source_quote: On October 23, 2025, WULF Compute LLC (“WULF Compute”), a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of TeraWulf Inc. ... completed its previously announced private offering of 7.750% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 (the “notes”). ... The aggregate principal amount of notes sold in the offering was $3.2 billion.

decisions.counterparty: None named; subsidiary-level disclosure (Google and certain other subsidiaries). Trustee for the notes is The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., but the $75.6B is not tied to the notes.
decisions.recourse: Not applicable — not an issuer debt obligation. Disclosed within a structural-subordination risk factor regarding subsidiary liabilities; leases have not commenced and are off-balance-sheet.
decisions.rationale: The $75.6B is aggregate FUTURE lease payments on data-center leases that have NOT yet commenced and are NOT yet recorded on the balance sheet, with only 'a portion' ever becoming finance-lease obligations — not issued notes, a drawn/committed term loan, or a recognized finance-lease principal; the issuer's only stated committed finance-lease balance is a separate $2.2B.
decisions.source_quote: Additionally, as of March 31, 2026, we have entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $75.6 billion, that are not yet recorded on our consolidated balance sheets, a portion of which will represent finance lease obligations.

decisions.counterparty: Alphabet Inc. (issuer); $58.475B figure relates to unnamed third-party data-center lessors, not a financing agent
decisions.recourse: None as committed debt; figure is off-balance-sheet future lease-payment commitment for not-yet-commenced leases, only an unquantified portion of which would ever become finance-lease obligations
decisions.rationale: The $58.475B is undiscounted future lease payments for not-yet-commenced data-center leases, explicitly not recorded on the balance sheet and only a portion of which will be finance-lease debt; it is an aggregate commitment figure, not a specific committed debt obligation. The filing's actual committed debt (the new notes) has only blank placeholder amounts in this preliminary supplement.
decisions.source_quote: Additionally, as of December 31, 2025, we have entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $58.475 billion, that are not yet recorded on our consolidated balance sheets, a portion of which will represent finance lease obligations.

decisions.counterparty: Alphabet Inc. (issuer); no lessor/agent named for the $42.6B figure
decisions.recourse: N/A — not a committed debt obligation; the $42.6B is uncommenced, unrecorded future lease payments, only a portion of which would become finance-lease (recourse) obligations once leases commence
decisions.rationale: The $42.6B basis is an aggregate of future lease payments for data-center leases that have NOT yet commenced and are NOT yet on the balance sheet, only 'a portion' of which will be finance leases — not a specific committed debt obligation; the filing's actual committed debt is the separate EUR 6.5B notes issuance for general corporate purposes.
decisions.source_quote: Additionally, as of September 30, 2025, we have entered into leases primarily related to data centers that have not yet commenced with future lease payments of $42.6 billion, that are not yet recorded on our consolidated balance sheets, a portion of which will represent finance lease obligations.

decisions.counterparty: Equinix Europe 2 Financing Corporation LLC (issuer/subsidiary), guaranteed by Equinix, Inc.; underwriters per Nov 5, 2025 underwriting agreement
decisions.recourse: Senior unsecured; fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Equinix, Inc. on an unsecured basis
decisions.rationale: Basis ~$141.55B appears nowhere in filing (an inflated synthetic aggregate; largest real figure is total long-term debt $18.6B / total capitalization $32.8B). The notes 'offered hereby' are a preliminary C$ supplement with principal left BLANK and shown as '—' in the capitalization table, so no specific committed amount. The only specific, already-issued committed debt with a stated dollar amount is the $1.25B 4.600% Senior Notes due 2030; verified to that committed part only.
decisions.source_quote: On November 13, 2025, Equinix Europe 2 Financing Corporation LLC ("Equinix Europe 2 Finco"), a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of Equinix, Inc., issued and sold $1,250,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 4.600% Senior Notes due 2030 (the "4.600% Senior Notes due 2030"), fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Equinix, Inc., pursuant to an underwriting agreement dated November 5, 2025 among Equinix Europe 2 Finco, Equinix, Inc. and the several underwriters named therein.

decisions.counterparty: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (Representative of Initial Purchasers); Wilmington Trust, National Association (Trustee and Collateral Agent)
decisions.recourse: Senior secured obligations of the Issuer (Hut 8 DC LLC, indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp.) and HoldCo (Hut 8 DC Member LLC); secured by/limited to the River Bend Data Center Project (245 MW), non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp. at the parent level (SPV-level project financing).
decisions.rationale: Genuine issued, committed AI/data-center debt — 6.192% Senior Secured Notes due 2042 completed/sold with an executed indenture — but the real committed principal is $3.25B, not the inflated $32.912B basis; verified amount set to the committed principal actually sold.
decisions.source_quote: The aggregate principal amount of Notes sold in the Offering was $3,250 million.

decisions.counterparty: Wilmington Trust, National Association (trustee and collateral agent); Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC (representative of initial purchasers); Issuer: APLD ComputeCo LLC
decisions.recourse: Senior secured obligations of the Issuer (APLD ComputeCo LLC) guaranteed by the Subsidiary Guarantors; secured by collateral on the ELN-02/ELN-03 Facilities/Projects; Applied Digital Corporation provides a customary completion guarantee. Notes issued at 97.000% of principal; 9.250% per annum, maturing December 15, 2030.
decisions.rationale: Completed private offering of 9.250% Senior Secured Notes due 2030 with a specific aggregate principal amount of $2.35 billion issued/closed on Nov 20, 2025 to fund construction of the ELN-02/ELN-03 Ellendale data centers - genuine committed, issued AI-infrastructure debt of the issuer.
decisions.source_quote: The aggregate principal amount of notes sold in the offering was $2.35 billion.

decisions.counterparty: APLD ComputeCo LLC (Issuer); Applied Digital Corporation (parent)
decisions.recourse: N/A - no such obligation exists in the filing
decisions.rationale: The $35,559,499,998 basis is an inflated aggregate that appears nowhere in the filing. The only specific committed debt in this 8-K is the same $2.35 billion 9.250% Senior Secured Notes (rate 9.250% per annum) already credited to row 308b0c6b7ceff944; there is no separate $35.5B committed obligation, so excluded to avoid double-counting an inflated rollup.
decisions.source_quote: The notes are senior secured obligations of the Issuer and bear interest at a rate of 9.250% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on June 15 and December 15 of each year, beginning on June 15, 2026.

decisions.counterparty: Goldman Sachs Bank USA (Administrative Agent); Lenders party to the Bridge Loan Credit Agreement
decisions.recourse: Unsecured, full recourse to Borrower (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.) plus Continuing Guaranty by the Guarantors party hereto (Article X), each guarantor's liability capped by a customary fraudulent-conveyance savings clause. No Collateral Agent, Security Agreement, Pledge Agreement or Mortgage exists in the document (0 occurrences); pricing references 'unsecured, long-term indebtedness for borrowed money of the Borrower.'
decisions.rationale: Binding committed $20B term-loan (Bridge) facility per a Mar 2, 2026 Bridge Loan Credit Agreement; Lenders severally agree to make the Loans with Aggregate Commitments of exactly $20,000,000,000 on the Closing Date - genuine committed debt of the issuer, not a shelf/resale, capacity, asset value, or seller-revenue figure. Proceeds refinance Existing Subsidiary Indebtedness (X Tranche B Term Loans, X.AI Term Loans and X.AI Notes), tying it to the AI-infrastructure debt stack.
decisions.source_quote: The Borrower has requested that the Lenders extend credit to it in the form of a term loan credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of $20,000,000,000 (the "Bridge Facility"). ... "Aggregate Commitments" means, on any date, the Commitments of all the Lenders as of such date. The aggregate principal amount of the Aggregate Commitments in effect on the Closing Date is TWENTY BILLION and No/100 DOLLARS ($20,000,000,000.00).

decisions.counterparty: None — no financing counterparty exists; figure is an internal executive-compensation goal. (Convertible-note holder Coatue LP appears only in a beneficial-ownership footnote with no dollar amount.)
decisions.recourse: None — no debt instrument, no obligor, no guarantee, no recourse scope; this is a hypothetical lease-contract-value metric, not a borrowing.
decisions.rationale: The $14B is the 500 MW maximum incentive-pay goal expressed as hypothetical AI-data-center-lease 'contract value' at prevailing market rates — an aggregate/aspirational capacity figure in a DEF 14A, not any issued note, committed term loan, or finance-lease principal of the issuer.
decisions.source_quote: With respect to Additional MW Expansion : The target 200 MW goal represented over $5.5 billion in contract value, and the 500 MW maximum goal represents approximately $14 billion in contract value based on prevailing market rates for AI data center leases.

decisions.counterparty: MUFG and Morgan Stanley (co-structuring agents and joint bookrunners); Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan (additional coordinating lead arrangers); anchored by Blackstone Credit & Insurance
decisions.recourse: Non-recourse; secured by substantially all assets of CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC (special-purpose subsidiary), not full recourse to CoreWeave, Inc.
decisions.rationale: The $8.5B is the maximum total borrowing CAPACITY of a delayed-draw term loan, not a drawn/committed principal: the filing explicitly frames it as 'up to ~$7.5B initially' rising to '$8.5 billion total borrowing capacity' only as assets stabilize -- a capacity 'up to' figure, not a specific committed obligation.
decisions.source_quote: The structure enables CoreWeave to borrow up to approximately $7.5 billion initially, with the ability to increase total borrowing capacity  to $8.5 billion as underlying assets reach stabilization.

decisions.counterparty: Fluidstack (lease supported by Google's credit)
decisions.recourse: n/a - lessor revenue, not issuer debt
decisions.rationale: The $12.8B is the aggregate contractual VALUE of long-term HPC lease agreements TeraWulf entered as LESSOR (revenue it is contracted to receive from customers), not committed debt of the issuer; it is also an aggregate 'in excess of' figure, not a specific committed obligation. The filing's actual debt line is a separate ~$6.5B blended debt-and-equity-linked figure.
decisions.source_quote: Execution of HPC lease agreements - Entered into long-term HPC lease agreements representing aggregate contractual value in excess of $12.8 billion, including a lease with Fluidstack supported by Google's credit.

decisions.counterparty: IREN Limited (issuer); placement agents Citigroup Global Markets Inc., Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC; initial purchasers of the Concurrent Offering
decisions.recourse: N/A - no such obligation; convertible notes (when/if issued) stated to be unsecured with no meaningful restrictive covenants
decisions.rationale: The $76,998,700,000 basis appears NOWHERE in the filing in any form (0 matches); it is a fabricated/inflated aggregate. The instrument is a preliminary, unpriced (rate is a blank '%') equity prospectus supplement plus a separate, non-consummated Concurrent Offering of convertible notes — no committed debt of this magnitude exists and the 'need' rate evidence is absent for the new notes.
decisions.source_quote: Concurrently with this offering, we are offering $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of % convertible senior notes due 2032 (the “2032 notes”) and $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of % convertible senior notes due 2033 ... that the initial purchasers of the Concurrent Offering have the options to purchase from us (the “Concurrent Offering”).

decisions.counterparty: IREN Limited (issuer); initial purchasers of the Concurrent Offering (made via separate confidential offering memorandum)
decisions.recourse: Convertible notes, if issued, stated to be unsecured; indentures contain no meaningful restrictive covenants
decisions.rationale: The $1.0 billion is an 'aggregate principal amount ... we are offering' figure for convertible senior notes in a preliminary (SUBJECT TO COMPLETION, Dec 1 2025) offering that is explicitly not consummated ('you should not assume that the Concurrent Offering ... will be consummated ... if at all'), made via a separate confidential offering memorandum and not this prospectus, with a still-blank '%' coupon. It is an offering-capacity / 'up to' aggregate, not a drawn or bindingly-committed obligation, so it is excluded.
decisions.source_quote: Additionally, in the Concurrent Offering, we are offering $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of % convertible senior notes due 2032 and $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of % convertible senior notes due 2033 ... Accordingly, you should not assume that the Concurrent Offering or the Repurchase will be consummated on the terms described in this prospectus supplement, if at all.

decisions.counterparty: None named (private offering to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A; initial purchasers unnamed)
decisions.recourse: N/A — proposed unsecured general senior obligations, not yet issued or committed
decisions.rationale: Filing is a press release announcing a PROPOSED $3.0B convertible notes offering 'subject to market and other conditions' with terms/rate to be set at pricing — an intended offering-capacity figure, not issued or bindingly-committed debt; basis $33.36B does not appear anywhere in the filing.
decisions.source_quote: CoreWeave, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV) (“CoreWeave”) today announced its intention to offer, subject to market and other conditions, $3.0 billion aggregate principal amount of its convertible senior notes due 2032 (the “Notes”) in a private offering.

decisions.counterparty: Initial purchasers / qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A (option counterparties for capped calls unnamed); no agent named
decisions.recourse: Unsecured senior obligations of MARA Holdings, Inc. (full recourse to issuer, unsecured)
decisions.rationale: Only $950M of issued 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2032 is genuine committed debt (closed/issued); the $19.35B basis is an unsupported inflated aggregate, and the $200M purchaser option plus $19.4M repurchase of existing 2026 notes are not new committed financing. Explicit rate: 0.00%, no accretion, only discretionary 'special interest' as sole remedy for reporting failures.
decisions.source_quote: MARA Holdings, Inc. (“MARA” or the “Company”), a leading digital energy and infrastructure company, today announced the closing on July 25, 2025 of its upsized offering of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2032 (the “notes”). The aggregate principal amount of the notes sold in the offering was $950 million.

decisions.counterparty: Bank of America, N.A. (Global Administrative Agent); various lenders and agents
decisions.recourse: Recourse to Prologis, L.P. (Operating Partnership), which unconditionally guarantees all borrower obligations; Prologis, Inc. not required to guarantee unless it incurs/guarantees new indebtedness. Cross-acceleration trigger >$150,000,000.
decisions.rationale: The only substantive figure is a revolving credit facility's aggregate 'up to' program capacity (~$3B plus $1B accordion), with tranche sizings being borrowing availability, not drawn or bindingly-committed term debt; no drawn balance, no notes issued, and not AI-infrastructure. The $16.5B basis does not appear in the filing.
decisions.source_quote: Pursuant to the 2026 Global Facility, the Operating Partnership and various affiliates thereof (collectively the “Borrowers”) may obtain loans and/or procure the issuance of letters of credit in various currencies on a revolving basis in an aggregate amount not exceeding the U.S. Dollar equivalent of approximately $3,000,000,000 (subject to increase by not more than the U.S. Dollar equivalent of $1,000,000,000 (determined as of the effective date of such increase) pursuant to the accordion feature included in the 2026 Global Facility).

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuing subsidiary of TeraWulf Inc.); these are the '2030 senior secured notes'. TeraWulf's general debt-securities indenture trustee is Wilmington Trust Company, N.A., though the filing names that trustee only for TeraWulf Inc. shelf debt securities, not specifically for these subsidiary notes.
decisions.recourse: Subsidiary-level senior secured notes at WULF Compute LLC, secured and structurally separate from TeraWulf's parent-level $2.5B convertible notes; filing does not label them non-recourse to TeraWulf but locates the obligation at the WULF Compute subsidiary.
decisions.rationale: Specific stated outstanding principal balance of issued senior secured notes funding HPC/data-center (AI) infrastructure -- a genuine committed debt obligation with an exact dollar figure, not a shelf/resale, capacity, UPB, or seller-revenue figure.
decisions.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025, the outstanding principal balance of the 2030 senior secured notes was $3,200.0 million.

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuer/obligor subsidiary of TeraWulf Inc.); no external indenture trustee or collateral agent named in this prospectus
decisions.recourse: Senior secured notes issued at the WULF Compute LLC subsidiary level (secured, 'senior secured'); recourse to WULF Compute LLC and its data-center collateral, included in consolidated TeraWulf total debt of $5.8 billion
decisions.rationale: Filing states the $3.2B as outstanding 'senior secured notes at WULF Compute LLC,' an issued/committed debt obligation with a specific dollar amount that is part of the company's actual total debt as of March 31, 2026 — not a capacity, shelf, or revenue figure. Google/Fluidstack relationship is separate lease-revenue credit support, not this debt.
decisions.source_quote: As of March 31, 2026, we had cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $3.1 billion and total debt of $5.8 billion, comprised of $2.5 billion of convertible notes at TeraWulf, $3.2 billion of senior secured notes at WULF Compute LLC, and $100 million of delayed-draw bridge loans at TeraWulf's Kentucky subsidiaries.

decisions.counterparty: Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (joint lead arrangers and bookrunners); facility issued through CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC
decisions.recourse: Asset-backed (HPC/GPU-backed) financing issued through a special-purpose financing subsidiary, CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC; structured as secured, syndicated debt aligned to the GPU infrastructure assets, indicating limited recourse to the CoreWeave parent rather than full corporate recourse.
decisions.rationale: Filing explicitly states CoreWeave has CLOSED a specific $3.1B delayed draw term loan facility (DDTL 5.0) to fund AI/GPU infrastructure for committed customer contracts; a closed, bindingly-committed DDTL with a specific dollar amount qualifies as committed AI-infrastructure debt.
decisions.source_quote: CoreWeave, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV), The Essential Cloud for AI™, today announced it has closed its $3.1 billion delayed draw term loan facility (“DDTL 5.0 Facility”), supporting continued expansion of its AI cloud platform and committed customer deployments.

decisions.counterparty: Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (joint lead arrangers and bookrunners); facility issued through CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC
decisions.recourse: Issued through special-purpose financing subsidiary CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC; HPC/GPU-collateralized syndicated term loan structured to align with the useful life of the underlying GPU assets, indicating asset-backed, limited recourse rather than unsecured parent recourse.
decisions.rationale: Same $3.1B closed DDTL 5.0 facility as the prior row; it is a specific, bindingly-committed (closed) delayed draw term loan for AI infrastructure, so it counts as committed AI-infrastructure debt rather than an aggregate or capacity figure.
decisions.source_quote: The DDTL 5.0 Facility has a maturity of approximately 5.5 years and was issued through CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC. The facility is structured as a delayed draw term loan designed to align funding with the deployment schedule and useful life of the underlying GPU infrastructure assets.

decisions.counterparty: Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (joint lead arrangers and bookrunners); borrower/issuer entity CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC
decisions.recourse: Limited/asset-backed recourse: the facility is issued through the bankruptcy-remote special-purpose subsidiary CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC, is HPC/GPU-collateral-backed, and is structured against the underlying GPU infrastructure assets, indicating recourse is to the SPV and its pledged AI infrastructure rather than full corporate recourse to CoreWeave, Inc.; no explicit parent guarantee is stated in the filing.
decisions.rationale: The $3.1B DDTL 5.0 Facility is explicitly closed (committed) and dedicated to AI/GPU infrastructure; it is a specific committed term-loan obligation, and the filing identifies the issuing SPV and arrangers, supporting it as genuine committed AI-infrastructure debt with limited recourse.
decisions.source_quote: The DDTL 5.0 Facility has a maturity of approximately 5.5 years and was issued through CoreWeave Financing DDTL V, LLC. The facility is structured as a delayed draw term loan designed to align funding with the deployment schedule and useful life of the underlying GPU infrastructure assets.

decisions.counterparty: APLD ComputeCo LLC (issuer/subsidiary); Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation named only as admin agent on the to-be-repaid existing SMBC credit facility, not on these Notes
decisions.recourse: Proposed Notes would be non-recourse to parent for principal (guaranteed only by APLD Compute's own subsidiaries the ELN-02/ELN-03 HoldCos/LandCos, secured by first-priority liens on APLD Compute and Guarantor assets and equity); parent provides only customary completion guarantees. But moot: nothing is yet committed.
decisions.rationale: Press release announces a PROPOSED, condition-subject 144A offering ('intends to offer... subject to market conditions'; 'no assurance as to whether, when or on what terms the offering may be completed') -- no notes issued/priced, so no committed debt; and the $4.7B basis is unsupported (only figure in filing is $2.35B).
decisions.source_quote: Applied Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: APLD) ... today announced that its subsidiary, APLD ComputeCo LLC ('APLD Compute'), intends to offer, subject to market conditions and other factors, $2.35 billion aggregate principal amount of senior secured notes due 2030 (the 'Notes'), in a private offering to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers in reliance on Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended.

decisions.counterparty: Issuer: APLD ComputeCo LLC (subsidiary of Applied Digital Corp.); Guarantors: APLD ELN-02/ELN-03 HoldCo, LLC and LandCo entities. Prior Credit and Guaranty Agreement admin agent (being repaid): Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC).
decisions.recourse: Structurally siloed / limited recourse: notes issued by APLD ComputeCo LLC and fully and unconditionally guaranteed only by APLD Compute's direct/indirect subsidiaries (the ELN-02/ELN-03 entities). Secured by first-priority liens on (i) substantially all assets of APLD Compute and the Guarantors (excluding certain excluded property), (ii) equity of the Guarantors, (iii) equity of APLD Compute held by APLD HPC Holdings 2 LLC, and (iv) the project accounts. Parent Applied Digital Corp. provides only customary completion guarantees, not full recourse for principal.
decisions.rationale: Only specific committed debt is the $2.35B senior secured notes priced by subsidiary APLD ComputeCo LLC; the $4.7B basis is an unsupported inflated aggregate (exactly 2x the $2.35B notes) with no support in the filing. Committed part set to the $2.35B note principal.
decisions.source_quote: Applied Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: APLD) ... today announced that its subsidiary, APLD ComputeCo LLC (“APLD Compute”), has priced a $2.35 billion offering (the “Offering”) of 9.250% senior secured notes due 2030 (the “Notes”) at an issue price of 97%.

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuer of senior secured notes); Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. (Administrative Agent/Lead Arranger for the uncommitted revolver); delayed-draw bridge loans at TeraWulf's Kentucky subsidiaries
decisions.recourse: Senior secured notes are obligations at WULF Compute LLC (subsidiary-level secured debt); delayed-draw bridge loans are at TeraWulf's Kentucky subsidiaries; the uncommitted $250M revolver would be secured by substantially all assets of TeraWulf and certain subsidiaries but is NOT yet committed.
decisions.rationale: Of the $3.55B basis, only the $3.2B senior secured notes plus $100M delivered delayed-draw bridge loans are genuine committed/outstanding debt; the $250M revolver is excluded as it is only an allocation 'subject to negotiation of and finalizing documentation and other closing conditions' (uncommitted 'up to' capacity).
decisions.source_quote: As of March 31, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $3.1 billion and total debt of $5.8 billion, comprised of $2.5 billion of convertible notes at TeraWulf, $3.2 billion of senior secured notes at WULF Compute LLC, and $100 million of delayed-draw bridge loans at TeraWulf's Kentucky subsidiaries.

decisions.counterparty: WULF Compute LLC (issuer subsidiary); 2030 senior secured notes
decisions.recourse: Issued/outstanding senior SECURED notes at the WULF Compute LLC subsidiary level, secured by subsidiary collateral; structurally senior at the subsidiary (TeraWulf parent-level debtholders are structurally subordinated to WULF Compute creditors). Specific stated outstanding principal, not parent-guaranteed shelf capacity.
decisions.rationale: Footnote (1) to the Capitalization table states the 2030 senior secured notes had an outstanding principal balance of exactly $3,200.0 million; the cover/Recent Developments narrative independently confirms '$3.2 billion of senior secured notes at WULF Compute LLC' as part of actual total debt of $5.8B as of 3/31/2026 — issued, drawn, specific-dollar committed AI-infrastructure (HPC/AI data center) debt, not a shelf/capacity/asset figure.
decisions.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025, the outstanding principal balance of the 2030 senior secured notes was $3,200.0 million.

decisions.counterparty: Issuer/obligor: WULF Compute LLC (wholly-owned subsidiary of TeraWulf Inc.); Guarantors: La Lupa Data LLC, Akela Data Holdings LLC, Akela Data LLC; Sole Bookrunner: Morgan Stanley
decisions.recourse: Secured + guaranteed. First-priority liens on substantially all assets of WULF Compute and the Guarantors, all WULF Compute equity held by TeraWulf Brookings LLC, a Fluidstack USA I Inc. lockbox account, and a pre-completion Google LLC warrant pledge; fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the named Guarantors; TeraWulf provides a completion guarantee for the Data Center Expansion.
decisions.rationale: Specific $3.2B principal of 7.750% senior secured notes due 2030 PRICED at par to finance AI/HPC data-center expansion (Lake Mariner) — issued/committed secured debt with a specific dollar amount, not an aggregate capacity, shelf/resale, UPB, or seller revenue.
decisions.source_quote: its wholly-owned subsidiary, WULF Compute LLC (“WULF Compute”), has priced a $3.2 billion offering (the “Offering”) of 7.750% senior secured notes due 2030 (the “Notes”) at par.

decisions.counterparty: Google (backstop provider); Fluidstack (tenant whose obligations are backstopped); TeraWulf / WULF Compute (issuer)
decisions.recourse: Non-recourse to TeraWulf as debt; the $1.8Bn is a Google-provided backstop/guarantee of Fluidstack's lease obligations in support of project debt, not an obligation of the issuer
decisions.rationale: The $1.8Bn is Google's backstop/guarantee of tenant Fluidstack's obligations 'in support of project debt' — not an issued note, drawn/committed term loan, or finance-lease principal of the issuer; the underlying project debt itself carries no stated specific committed dollar amount.
decisions.source_quote: Google to provide $1.8Bn backstop of Fluidstack obligations in support of project debt

decisions.counterparty: Fluidstack (tenant); Google (backstop provider)
decisions.recourse: No issuer recourse debt. The $1.8Bn is a Google guarantee/backstop of Fluidstack's tenant lease obligations 'in Support of Project Debt' — not a debt obligation of the issuer TeraWulf.
decisions.rationale: The $1.8Bn is a third-party (Google) backstop of the tenant's (Fluidstack's) lease obligations under a 10-yr ~$3.7Bn hyperscale lease (seller-side contracted revenue), not issued notes, a drawn/committed term loan, or finance-lease principal of TeraWulf; TeraWulf's only genuine issued debt here is the separate $500M Convertible Notes, not this figure.
decisions.source_quote: $1.8Bn Google Backstop of Fluidstack Obligations in Support of Project Debt

decisions.counterparty: Initial purchasers under Rule 144A (qualified institutional buyers); notes are senior unsecured obligations of Akamai Technologies, Inc.
decisions.recourse: Senior unsecured full-recourse obligation of Akamai Technologies, Inc. (issuer-level, not project-ring-fenced)
decisions.rationale: Priced private offering of $1.5B aggregate principal of 0.25% convertible senior notes due 2033 -- a specific, committed issuer debt obligation with stated terms and a fixed close date; the separate $225M purchaser option is contingent capacity and is excluded.
decisions.source_quote: today announced that it has priced its private offering of $1.5 billion in aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2033.

decisions.counterparty: Initial purchasers (QIBs under Rule 144A); Option Counterparties for hedge/warrant transactions (unnamed)
decisions.recourse: N/A — no committed obligation; if priced, notes would be senior unsecured obligations of Akamai with no AI-infrastructure security or use

deduped_distinct_instruments.method: Canonical instrument-level de-duplication of the 39 adversarially-confirmed committed rows (0 refuted). AI-linkage classed: core_cluster (neocloud/crypto-AI compute), datacenter_infra (colo/REIT/CDN general corporate notes), questionable_linkage (SpaceX bridge facility = space, not AI data centers -- excluded from headline).
